key: The partial becomes complete; the crooked, straight; the empty, full; the worn out, new.
s: Reversals open a chapter on the sage free from self-display; Wang Bi, on chapter 22, reads them as not displaying oneself, not holding oneself right, not boasting and not vaunting oneself, which leave one whole, one’s rightness plain, one’s merit kept and one’s virtue lasting.
src: Wang Bi, Laozi zhu, chapter 22, zh.wikisource (the Huating Zhang edition), revision 2354026 (2024)

opened.edition: zh.wikisource 道德經 (王弼本), the 華亭張氏 edition, revision 2354026
opened.locator: chapter 22, comments on 曲則全, 枉則直, 窪則盈 and 敝則新

evidence.words: 不自見其明則全也。 … 不自是則其是彰也。 … 不自伐則其功有也。 … 不自矜則其德長也。
evidence.gloss: (On the partial becoming complete:) not displaying his own brightness, he is whole. (On the crooked becoming straight:) not holding himself right, his rightness is made plain. (On the empty becoming full:) not boasting of himself, his merit remains. (On the worn out becoming new:) not vaunting himself, his virtue grows long.
